title: SBI Funds Management IPO Draws $31 Billion in Bids, Becoming India's Fourth-Most-Subscribed Offering
excerpt: India's largest asset manager raised over $1 billion in the country's biggest IPO of the year, with anchor investors including BlackRock and sovereign wealth funds from Singapore, Abu Dhabi and Norway signalling confidence in India's booming mutual fund market.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • SBI Funds Management drew bids worth ₹3 trillion ($31.14 billion) in its $1.03 billion IPO.
  • The offering became India's fourth-most-subscribed IPO ever.
  • Anchor investors include BlackRock and sovereign wealth funds from Singapore, Abu Dhabi and Norway.
  • The IPO marks a comeback for India's primary market after a subdued first half.
  • Shares begin trading on July 21.
SBI Funds Management, India's largest asset manager, drew bids worth ₹3 trillion ($31.14 billion) in its initial public offering, making it the country's fourth-most-subscribed IPO on record, [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/indias-sbi-funds-management-draws-31-billion-countrys-fourth-most-bid-ipo-2026-07-17/). The $1.03 billion offering, which closed on Thursday, marks the biggest listing on Indian exchanges so far in 2026 and signals a strong recovery for the primary market after a subdued first half driven by concerns over crude oil prices and global uncertainty. ## Institutional Appetite Demand was overwhelmingly institutional. Qualified institutional buyers bid for $25 billion worth of shares — 140 times the number allocated to them, according to exchange data. The company had already raised $278.5 million from anchor investors ahead of the public launch, a roster that included BlackRock and sovereign wealth funds from Singapore, Abu Dhabi and Norway. The retail investor portion was subscribed 3.6 times, while the segment reserved for SBI shareholders saw 9.5 times subscription. SBI Funds Management is a joint venture between State Bank of India (SBI), the country's largest lender, and Amundi, Europe's largest asset manager. As of March 2026, the firm managed funds worth ₹12.5 trillion ($131 billion), making it the dominant player in India's rapidly growing mutual fund industry. ## The Bigger Picture The IPO's success stands behind only the public offerings of Reliance Power, LG Electronics India and Bajaj Housing Finance in terms of total bids received, according to data from PRIME Database. The offering at ₹574 per share reflects investor confidence in India's asset management sector, which has benefited from a structural shift in household savings patterns. Indian equity mutual funds have recorded 64 consecutive months of inflows through June 2026, with systematic investment plans (SIPs) becoming the preferred route for millions of retail investors. India's primary market pipeline remains busy. Mega listings from Reliance Jio and the National Stock Exchange are expected before year-end, and the SBI Funds IPO may set the tone for how those offerings are received. ## What NRI Investors Should Know For the diaspora, SBI Funds Management is a familiar name — SBI's extensive distribution network extends to NRI banking channels, and many overseas Indians hold SBI mutual fund investments. The IPO underscores a maturing Indian capital market where asset management companies are now large enough to command global institutional interest. Shares are expected to begin trading on July 21. Analysts at Aditya Birla Money noted that the firm's market leadership, strong distribution network and robust profitability position it well for the listing.
